title: The Slow Orbit
premise: Wren Dravenmoor, a cargo navigator on the colony ship Meridian's Wake, discovers that the shared dream infecting the colony's children is a distress signal from the cryosleep backups in his own hold — twelve thousand sleeping colonists whose minds are waking without bodies. The colony council, led by Wren's former lover Captain Ilsa Voss, wants to terminate the backups to save power for the living; Wren, who carries fragmented memories of being one of them once, believes they can be restored into the failing terraforming shells. As sabotage and mutiny fracture the crew, Wren learns the dream was sent by his own discarded first self. In the end, he sacrifices his place among the waking — merging with his backup to become the bridge consciousness that guides half of humanity home, while the other half sleeps on toward a second chance.
about_author: Yara Nystrom is a former maritime cartographer who traded sea charts for star charts and now writes from a converted lighthouse on the Norwegian coast. Her fiction explores what survives when memory becomes negotiable.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Five years into hauling freight through contested orbits around the half-terraformed colony of Vesperine, Wren logs another routine jump past the hold where twelve thousand cryo-backups sleep. He avoids that deck the way other men avoid graves. Emotional beat: quiet dread established; the reader learns he flinches at his own reflection.

chapters.title: The Children's Chorus
chapters.summary: POV Mara, a colony schoolteacher. Forty-seven children fall asleep mid-lesson and wake reciting coordinates no one taught them — coordinates matching the Meridian's Wake's hold. The council dismisses it as mass hysteria. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder curdling into institutional denial.

chapters.title: Summons
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Captain Ilsa Voss — the woman he loved before she took command — orders him to investigate the dream, knowing his history with the backup program. Descending into the hold for the first time in five years, he hears the children's coordinates spoken back to him by the sleep monitors. Emotional beat: dread made intimate.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Decrypting the signal, Wren finds it signed with his own name — not his current one, but the identity he surrendered when he was decanted five years ago. His 'original' is awake inside the network, dreaming outward through the children. Emotional beat: identity crisis; the ground tilts under everything he believes about himself.

chapters.title: Council of the Living
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The council votes to purge the backups: power reserves are failing, and the sleepers' waking minds are draining the grid. Ilsa argues survival of the embodied; Wren pleads for restoration into the empty terraforming shells. The vote goes against him. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth splits old lovers down the middle.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Someone begins killing the backups early — coolant lines cut, pods cycling to flush. Wren suspects engineer Dov Kestrel, who lost family to the original colonization and hates the sleepers as dead weight. A child slips aboard seeking 'the man in the dream.' Emotional beat: paranoia and protectiveness entwined.

chapters.title: The First Self
chapters.summary: POV Wren, deep-link. Wren jacks into the hold network and meets his original — patient, wounded, and honest about why Wren was created: a disposable body so the real man could survive the accident that killed the first crew. The original asks not to be saved, but to be chosen. Emotional beat: grief and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Mutiny at Periapsis
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Kestrel's faction seizes engineering to force the purge before the grid collapses; Ilsa must choose between her command and her conscience. She releases the evidence Wren found — that the colony itself was built on the backs of people never told they'd be backups. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted; loyalty realigned with truth.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Climax. With hours of power left, there is only enough energy to restore either the twelve thousand sleepers or keep the colony's failing atmosphere processors alive. Wren offers the third path: merge with his original to become a distributed consciousness that can run both systems at reduced capacity — at the cost of ever being wholly himself again. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship of identity.

chapters.title: Slow Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Mara, coda. The children stop dreaming; the sleepers wake slowly into shells above Vesperine; the colony endures on borrowed light. Mara visits Wren — present but plural, speaking sometimes in two voices — and finds him at peace, watching the ships come down. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; identity survived by being shared.
